title: Breaker Vex, a Mega Man X-Inspired Action Platformer
author: Cautious_Material_40
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I've been working on a game called **Breaker Vex**, a 2D action platformer inspired by Mega Man X, with fast-paced combat, exploration, boss fights, and some Metroidvania elements.

I'm developing it solo with basically zero prior game dev experience, using AI to handle all of the coding in Unity. My process has been a lot of experimenting, testing, tweaking, and figuring things out as I go.

I've also been using Mega Man X assets as temporary placeholders while commissioning custom pixel art and animations to give the game its own identity. It's been really cool seeing everything gradually come together.

I've spent a ton of time refining the movement, combat mechanics, and overall gameplay. There's still a lot of work ahead, but I recently put together a trailer showing where things stand.

I'm curious how this looks to everyone else.

**Does the gameplay look fun? How's the trailer?**

Would love some honest feedback!

replies.author: Cautious_Material_40
replies.body:
I get where you're coming from, and I appreciate you checking out the trailer and saying the gameplay looks cool!

Mega Man X is absolutely a massive inspiration here, and I'm not trying to hide that. In fact, most of the enemies in the trailer are literally ripped from Mega Man X. I've been using those assets as placeholders while I learn how to build enemy AI, implement combat mechanics, and figure out what I'm actually capable of creating.

The main character was commissioned from an artist, but I definitely recognize the Mega Man X influence in his design too. That's something I'm aware of and can continue working on as the game develops.

I do think there's a distinction between using existing assets to learn and prototype a game versus trying to pass someone else's work off as your own finished product. I'm not claiming I've created something entirely original here, and I know those borrowed assets would need to be replaced if I take this toward a proper release.

Right now, I'm just a guy with basically zero game development experience, using AI to help me build a game inspired by something I grew up loving. I'm having a blast learning, experimenting, and seeing what I can actually make. A lot of this is about capturing that feeling I had playing games on the SNES as a kid while also adding my own spin to it.

I absolutely welcome criticism, and I appreciate your input!

And genuinely, I appreciate the offer to help with the designs! I'd actually love to see what you have in mind. If you've got some ideas for how to give the characters a more unique identity while still capturing that Mega Man X feel, I'm all ears. I'm always interested in seeing different creative perspectives, especially from people who have more experience with this stuff than I do!
